12	import type { Agent, AgentOptions } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
13	import type { Branded } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand'
14	import type { ContentBlock } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
15	import type { SessionEvent, SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
16	import type { ObjectJsonSchema, ToolRestriction } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'
17	import type { SubagentDescriptorData } from './descriptor.ts'
18	
19	/** Identifies one accepted subagent run across its lifecycle event pair. */
20	export type SubagentRunId = Branded<'SubagentRunId'>
21	
22	/**
23	 * Brand a string as a {@link SubagentRunId}.
24	 * @param id - the raw run id.
25	 * @returns the same string, branded.
26	 */
27	export function SubagentRunId(id: string): SubagentRunId {
28	  return id as SubagentRunId
29	}
30	
31	/**
32	 * Observe-only identifying detail for a published subagent run, carried by
33	 * `subagent/start`. One-shot runs and continuable Activation epochs share this
34	 * payload, so an observer sees the same vocabulary for both.
35	 */
36	export interface SubagentRunInfo {
37	  /** Unique identity shared with the paired terminal event. */
38	  readonly runId: SubagentRunId
39	  /**
40	   * Provider name recorded when the child was first created. The provider may
41	   * be absent when an accepted one-shot run becomes ready or a persisted
42	   * Activation cold-resumes, because neither lifecycle depends on continued
43	   * registration.
44	   */
45	  readonly provider: string
46	  /** The child agent's id. */
47	  readonly id: SessionId
48	  /** Snapshot of whether `SubagentRun.localAgent` was present when start fulfilled. */
49	  readonly local: boolean
50	}
51	
52	/**
53	 * Observe-only outcome detail for a settled subagent run, carried by
54	 * `subagent/end` and paired with one {@link SubagentRunInfo} by `runId`.
55	 */
56	export interface SubagentRunEndInfo {
57	  /** Unique identity shared with the paired start event. */
58	  readonly runId: SubagentRunId
59	  /** The same provider name carried by the paired start event. */
60	  readonly provider: string
61	  /** The child agent's id. */
62	  readonly id: SessionId
63	  /** Snapshot of whether `SubagentRun.localAgent` was present when start fulfilled. */
64	  readonly local: boolean
65	  /** The terminal stop reason. */
66	  readonly stopReason: SubagentResult['stopReason']
67	  /**
68	   * The child's final assistant output, selected by the same rule as
69	   * {@link SubagentResult.output}; absent on infrastructure rejection or when
70	   * the child produced none.
71	   */
72	  readonly lastAssistantMessage?: ContentBlock[]
73	}
74	
75	/**
76	 * Which START-TIME features a provider supports. Checked by the service before delegating to
77	 * {@link SubagentProvider.start}: a request that needs a capability the chosen provider lacks
78	 * is rejected with a typed error rather than accepted-then-ignored (the "fail loud, no silent
79	 * degradation" rule). These flags describe the ONE-SHOT
80	 * {@link SubagentProvider.start} path, where the provider composes the child;
81	 * continuable children are composed by the continuation manager itself and are
82	 * gated by {@link SubagentProvider.prepareContinuable} instead. Each flag
83	 * corresponds one-to-one to a {@link SubagentStartRequest} option: `depthLimit`
84	 * to `maxDepth`; the other names match.
85	 */
86	export interface SubagentCapabilities {
87	  readonly outputSchema: boolean
88	  readonly depthLimit: boolean
89	  readonly toolFilter: boolean
90	  readonly persona: boolean
91	}
92	
93	/**
94	 * What a caller asks for when starting a ONE-SHOT subagent. The tool layer
95	 * builds this from the model's `{ description, prompt }` plus its own config;
96	 * the service validates {@link SubagentCapabilities} against the named provider
97	 * and resolves the durable descriptor before dispatching to
98	 * {@link SubagentProvider.start}.
99	 */
100	export interface SubagentStartRequest {
101	  /** Optional short display label persisted with a session-backed child. */
102	  readonly label?: string
103	  /** Content delivered as the child's user message. */
104	  readonly prompt: ContentBlock[]
105	  /**
106	   * The spawning agent. In-process providers derive workspace, lineage, and
107	   * delegation depth from its durable session state. ACP reads only its cwd,
108	   * and only when no deployment `cwd` override is configured.
109	   */
110	  readonly parent: Agent
111	  /**
112	   * Cancellation signal from the spawning context (the tool's `exec.signal`).
113	   * This is the canonical cancellation channel both before and after startup:
114	   * a provider rejects `start()` after cleaning partial resources when it
115	   * fires before the run is published, and cancels the published run's
116	   * remaining turn work when it fires afterward.
117	   */
118	  readonly signal: AbortSignal
119	  readonly agentOptions?: AgentOptions
120	  /**
121	   * Object-rooted JSON Schema within `assertObjectJsonSchema`'s enforced subset. Start rejects
122	   * unsupported schemas or providers without the capability. Data must be plain host-realm JSON;
123	   * a successful child returns the matching value as {@link SubagentResult.structured}.
124	   */
125	  readonly outputSchema?: ObjectJsonSchema
126	  /**
127	   * Optional absolute delegation-depth cap for the child being started: its
128	   * computed depth must be less than or equal to this non-negative safe
129	   * integer. Requires {@link SubagentCapabilities.depthLimit}; rejected at
130	   * start otherwise.
131	   */
132	  readonly maxDepth?: number
133	  /**
134	   * Optional child tool scoping. Requires {@link SubagentCapabilities.toolFilter};
135	   * rejected at start otherwise. In-process backends apply it as a scoped
136	   * `tools.restrict()` in the child's creation window: the named tools vanish
137	   * from the child's prompt AND refuse to execute (one visibility), with loud
138	   * unknown-name validation.
139	   */
140	  readonly toolFilter?: ToolRestriction
141	  /**
142	   * Optional per-child persona. Requires {@link SubagentCapabilities.persona};
143	   * rejected at start otherwise. In-process backends register it as a scoped
144	   * `deployment:persona` section on the child, SHADOWING the deployment's
145	   * persona for this child alone — same template semantics as the deployment
146	   * persona (strict `{{…}}` interpolation against the registered variables).
147	   */
148	  readonly persona?: string
149	}
150	
151	/**
152	 * Provider-facing one-shot request after {@link SubagentRuntime.start} resolves
153	 * the durable child descriptor.
154	 */
155	export interface ResolvedSubagentStartRequest extends SubagentStartRequest {
156	  /** Detached descriptor a session-backed provider persists in the child log. */
157	  readonly descriptor: SubagentDescriptorData
158	}
159	
160	/**
161	 * What the continuation manager asks a provider for while materializing one
162	 * continuable child's FIRST activation. The manager has already reserved the
163	 * durable child identity and owns every later operation, so this request
164	 * carries only what distinguishes a fresh child from one seeded with parent
165	 * history.
166	 */
167	export interface ContinuableCreateRequest {
168	  /** The reserved durable child session id, for provider diagnostics. */
169	  readonly sessionId: SessionId
170	  /** The delegating parent agent whose history a seeding provider reads. */
171	  readonly parent: Agent
172	  /**
173	   * Caller cancellation, which owns preparation only until the manager accepts
174	   * the initial prompt into the child's inbox.
175	   */
176	  readonly signal: AbortSignal
177	}
178	
179	/**
180	 * A provider's detached contribution to one continuable child's creation. This
181	 * is DATA, never a capability: it carries no Agent, `AgentHandle`, prompt
182	 * delivery, result, disposal, or resume operation, because the continuation
183	 * manager owns the child's whole lifecycle after preparation.
184	 */
185	export interface ContinuableCreateSpec {
186	  /**
187	   * Completed-turn prefix of the parent's log to seed the child session with,
188	   * or absent for a fresh child. Same durable contract as
189	   * `CreateAgentOptions.seed`: contiguous from seq 0, lossless JSON, balanced.
190	   */
191	  readonly seed?: readonly SessionEvent[]
192	}
193	
194	/**
195	 * Why a subagent run ended. Merge-extensible (a backend may add variants);
196	 * consumers branch on the known cases and fall through `default`. The known
197	 * cases mirror the harness turn-end vocabulary so the tool layer can map a
198	 * non-`completed` result to an `isError` tool result.
199	 */
200	export interface SubagentStopReasonMap {
201	  /** The child finished its turn normally. */
202	  completed: 'completed'
203	  /** Cancelled through the request signal or disposal. */
204	  aborted: 'aborted'
205	  /** Model or transport failure. */
206	  error: 'error'
207	  /** The child hit its token ceiling before finishing. */
208	  'max-tokens': 'max-tokens'
209	  /** The child declined the task. */
210	  refusal: 'refusal'
211	}
212	
213	/** The union over {@link SubagentStopReasonMap} — widens automatically as backends merge in variants. */
214	export type SubagentStopReason = SubagentStopReasonMap[keyof SubagentStopReasonMap]
215	
216	/**
217	 * The terminal outcome of a subagent run, resolved by {@link SubagentRun.result}.
218	 */
219	export interface SubagentResult {
220	  /**
221	   * The child's final assistant output is the content of its last non-empty
222	   * assistant message. Empty-content messages, including usage-only messages,
223	   * are skipped. Without a non-empty message, the output is its accumulated
224	   * assistant text stream, or `[]` when the child produced neither.
225	   */
226	  readonly output: ContentBlock[]
227	  /**
228	   * The structured result after a requested `outputSchema` was successfully
229	   * satisfied. Requesting a schema does not guarantee presence: a provider can
230	   * end with `stopReason: 'error'` when the child fails or finishes without a
231	   * valid capture. The structured value is validated against the requested
232	   * output schema by the provider; `unknown` here because the seam is
233	   * schema-agnostic.
234	   */
235	  readonly structured?: unknown
236	  /** Why the run ended. A non-`completed` reason means `output` may be partial. */
237	  readonly stopReason: SubagentStopReason
238	}
239	
240	/**
241	 * ONE-SHOT child handle returned after publication. Prompt submission, turn
242	 * work, and infrastructure faults after that boundary belong to {@link result}.
243	 * Consumers await that result and must always {@link dispose} to cancel
244	 * remaining work and reach quiescence. A run is one disposable foreground
245	 * delegation with one result; continuable conversations have no run — the
246	 * continuation manager holds their `AgentHandle` directly and orders every
247	 * turn through the child's own inbox.
248	 */
249	export interface SubagentRun {
250	  /**
251	   * Parent-scoped run id. For a local run, this MUST equal the published child
252	   * session id, whose `parentSession` records `request.parent.session.id`; a
253	   * remote provider mints an id unique in the parent namespace.
254	   */
255	  readonly id: SessionId
256	  /**
257	   * The exact published in-process child, or `undefined` for a remote run.
258	   * When present, its id is {@link id}; the provider retains no ownership
259	   * implication beyond the run's ordinary {@link dispose} contract.
260	   */
261	  readonly localAgent: Agent | undefined
262	  /**
263	   * Resolves with the child's terminal {@link SubagentResult} when the run
264	   * settles. Does NOT reject on a child-level failure — a model/transport
265	   * failure resolves with `stopReason: 'error'` so the consumer maps it to an
266	   * `isError` tool result. Rejects on an infrastructure fault the seam cannot
267	   * represent as a stop reason.
268	   */
269	  readonly result: Promise<SubagentResult>
270	  /**
271	   * Cancel remaining work, reach child quiescence, and release resources.
272	   * Idempotent.
273	   */
274	  dispose(): Promise<void>
275	}
276	
277	/**
278	 * One registered transport for running child agents. Providers are trusted
279	 * same-process implementations; callers treat descriptors and returned values
280	 * as borrowed immutable data. The service may call one provider concurrently
281	 * for distinct children. Providers isolate operation-local mutable state; a
282	 * shared capacity controller may delay an operation but must not couple its
283	 * settlement or cleanup to a sibling.
284	 */
285	export interface SubagentProvider {
286	  /** Unique registry name (e.g. `spawn`, `fork`, `acp`). */
287	  readonly name: string
288	  /** The start-time features this provider supports (see {@link SubagentCapabilities}). */
289	  readonly capabilities: SubagentCapabilities
290	  /**
291	   * Whether the child sees the parent's completed-turn prefix. This is descriptive, not a
292	   * service-validated start capability: the model-facing tool derives truthful wording from it.
293	   * It says nothing about tool registration, injected services, or authority inheritance.
294	   */
295	  readonly inheritsParentContext: boolean
296	  /**
297	   * Establish a ONE-SHOT child and return its handle after publication.
298	   * The service has already validated that every requested start-time
299	   * capability is supported and resolved `request.descriptor`, so a
300	   * session-backed implementation appends that descriptor inside the child's
301	   * initial turn. Before fulfillment, the provider owns setup and cleans any
302	   * unpublished partial resources before rejecting. Ownership transfers on
303	   * fulfillment; subsequent turn or infrastructure failure settles through
304	   * the returned run. Distinct starts may overlap; cancellation, failure,
305	   * result settlement, and disposal remain independent for each run.
306	   */
307	  start(request: ResolvedSubagentStartRequest): Promise<SubagentRun>
308	  /**
309	   * OPTIONAL (continuable-creation capability): contribute the detached
310	   * creation inputs that distinguish this provider's continuable children —
311	   * only whether the child session is seeded with parent history. Method
312	   * presence IS the capability: the service rejects continuable starts on
313	   * providers without it, while a provider that has it may still serve
314	   * ordinary one-shot delegations.
315	   *
316	   * This is the provider's ONLY participation in a continuable child. The
317	   * continuation manager owns identity reservation, composition, Agent
318	   * creation, prompt delivery, cold resume, ownership, and disposal, so a
319	   * provider never sees the child's Agent, handle, turns, or teardown.
320	   * Distinct preparations may overlap; each follows its own signal and returns
321	   * data belonging only to `request.sessionId`.
322	   */
323	  prepareContinuable?(request: ContinuableCreateRequest): Promise<ContinuableCreateSpec>
324	}

1	# AGENTS.md
2	
3	DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.
4	
5	## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius
6	
7	**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` without a compatibility promise.
8	
9	## Repository layout
10	
11	```
12	vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
13	packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
14	  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
15	  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
...
26	  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
27	  context/     request-context plugins
28	  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
29	  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
30	  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
31	  todo/        todo_write tool
32	  plan/        plan mode as logged state
33	  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
34	  guard/       loop-hygiene, tool-timeout, session-budget plugins
35	  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
36	  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
37	  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
38	  identity/    anonymous identity
39	  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
40	  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
41	  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
42	  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
...
47	  util/        zero-dependency utilities
48	python/      Python SDK and bundled runtime (see python/README.md)
49	native/      @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run source of record (see native/README.md)
50	examples/    Runnable cordis.yml leaves over packages/examples bundles (see examples/AGENTS.md)
51	.agents/     Agent workflows and Agent Notes (`notes/`)
52	docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
53	scripts/     repo gates and generators
54	website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
55	data/        this repository's own transcripts, runs, knowledge packs (see data/README.md)

121	      executable,

125	      onError: (error, stopReason) => {

128	        )

296	      }
297	    }
298	    // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-unnecessary-condition -- the request can abort while process cleanup is awaited.
299	    if (cancelledBeforeCleanup || request.signal.aborted) {
300	      throw new Error('subagent-claude-code: request was aborted before SDK startup')
301	    }
302	    throw thrown(error)
303	  }
304	
305	  const publishedQuery = query
306	  const publishedChild = child
307	  const bridge = spec.bridge
308	  const result = settleRunResult({
309	    attempt: () => consumeClaudeQuery(publishedQuery, bridge?.observe.bind(bridge)),
310	    collectOutput: () => [],
311	    cancelled: () => controller.signal.aborted,
312	    onError: spec.onError,
313	    signal: request.signal,
314	    onAbort,
315	  }).then((settled) => {
316	    bridge?.settle(settled.stopReason)
317	    return settled
318	  })
319	
320	  return subprocessRunHandle({
321	    id: bridge?.id ?? SessionId(randomUUID()),
322	    ...bridge === undefined ? {} : { localAgent: bridge.agent },
323	    result,
324	    signal: request.signal,
325	    onAbort,
326	    requestCancel,
327	    teardown: async () => {
328	      try {
329	        await disposeClaudeCodeChild(publishedQuery, publishedChild)
330	      } finally {
331	        // The child agent and its served turn are released even when the CLI's
332	        // own teardown failed: the run's durable record must still close.
333	        await bridge?.release()
334	      }
335	    },
336	  })
337	}

20	const WINDOWS_BATCH_EXECUTABLE_ENV = 'DSH_CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE'

22	function thrown(value: unknown): Error {
23	  /* v8 ignore next -- the subprocess seam rejects with Error. */
24	  return value instanceof Error ? value : new Error(String(value))
25	}

27	/**
28	 * Encode the SDK's complete child environment as a subprocess overlay.
29	 * @param env - SDK-composed child environment after its removals and replacements.
30	 * @returns explicit values plus tombstones for surviving ambient names the SDK removed.
31	 */
32	export function sdkEnvironmentOverlay(
33	  env: SpawnOptions['env'],
34	): NodeJS.ProcessEnv {
35	  const overlay: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = { ...env }
36	  for (const name of Object.keys(scrubbedParentEnv())) {
37	    if (!(name in env)) overlay[name] = undefined
38	  }
39	  return overlay
40	}

42	/**
43	 * Translate one official SDK spawn request to the shared process owner.
44	 * @param options - command, arguments, workspace, environment, and forwarded signal from the SDK.
45	 * @param graceMs - process-tree termination grace.
46	 * @param platform - host platform selecting the Windows batch-shim boundary.
47	 * @returns the fully explicit shared subprocess request.
48	 * @remarks The batch-shim path quotes only the resolved executable. The pinned SDK
49	 * supplies fixed flag arguments without cmd metacharacters; cmd reparses that tail.
50	 */
51	export function claudeSpawnSpec(
52	  options: SpawnOptions,
53	  graceMs: number,
54	  platform: NodeJS.Platform = process.platform,
55	): SubprocessSpawnSpec {
56	  if (options.cwd === undefined || options.cwd.length === 0) {
57	    throw new Error('subagent-claude-code: SDK spawn request omitted its workspace')
58	  }
59	  const extension = extname(options.command).toLowerCase()
60	  const batchShim = platform === 'win32' && (extension === '.cmd' || extension === '.bat')
61	  const env = sdkEnvironmentOverlay(options.env)
62	  const argv = batchShim
63	    ? ['cmd.exe', '/d', '/v:off', '/s', '/c', `%${WINDOWS_BATCH_EXECUTABLE_ENV}%`, ...options.args]
64	    : [options.command, ...options.args]
65	  if (batchShim) env[WINDOWS_BATCH_EXECUTABLE_ENV] = `"${options.command}"`
66	  return {
67	    argv,
68	    cwd: options.cwd,
69	    stdio: { stdin: 'pipe', stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'inherit' },
70	    graceMs,
71	    signal: options.signal,
72	    env,
73	  }
74	}

76	/**
77	 * SDK-facing view of one shared managed process. Protocol transport remains
78	 * in the official SDK; this adapter only projects streams and exit events.
79	 */
80	export class ManagedClaudeCodeProcess implements SpawnedProcess {
81	  readonly stdin
82	  readonly stdout
83	  private readonly events = new EventEmitter()
84	  private exitCodeValue: number | null = null
85	  private signalCodeValue: NodeJS.Signals | null = null
86	  private killRequested = false
87	
88	  /**
89	   * Project a managed process with piped stdin and stdout.
90	   * @param child - shared handle that remains the process-tree authority.
91	   */
92	  constructor(private readonly child: SubprocessHandle) {
93	    this.stdin = child.stdin as NonNullable<SubprocessHandle['stdin']>
94	    this.stdout = child.stdout as NonNullable<SubprocessHandle['stdout']>
95	    // EventEmitter gives `error` special throw semantics without a listener.
96	    // The SDK attaches its listener synchronously after custom spawn returns,
97	    // while this no-op also contains an already-rejected spawn handle.
98	    this.events.on('error', () => {})
99	    void child.done.then(
100	      (outcome) => {
101	        this.exitCodeValue = outcome.exitCode
102	        this.signalCodeValue = outcome.signal
103	        this.events.emit('exit', outcome.exitCode, outcome.signal)
104	      },
105	      (error: unknown) => {
106	        this.events.emit('error', thrown(error))
107	      },
108	    )
109	  }
110	
111	  /** Whether the SDK has requested managed tree termination. */
112	  get killed(): boolean {
113	    return this.killRequested
114	  }
115	
116	  /** Direct-child exit code, or null while running or after signal exit. */
117	  get exitCode(): number | null {
118	    return this.exitCodeValue
119	  }
120	
121	  /** Direct-child terminating signal, if any. */
122	  get signalCode(): NodeJS.Signals | null {
123	    return this.signalCodeValue
124	  }
125	
126	  /**
127	   * Route the SDK's termination request to the tree-scoped process owner.
128	   * @param _signal - SDK-selected signal; the shared seam owns its escalation ladder.
129	   * @returns false only after exit or a previous termination request.
130	   */
131	  kill(_signal: NodeJS.Signals): boolean {
132	    if (
133	      this.killRequested
134	      || this.exitCodeValue !== null
135	      || this.signalCodeValue !== null
136	    ) {
137	      return false
138	    }
139	    this.killRequested = true
140	    this.child.terminate()
141	    return true
142	  }
143	
144	  /** Register a persistent process lifecycle listener. */
145	  on(
146	    event: 'exit' | 'error',
147	    listener: ((code: number | null, signal: NodeJS.Signals | null) => void)
148	      | ((error: Error) => void),
149	  ): void {
150	    this.events.on(event, listener)
151	  }
152	
153	  /** Register a one-shot process lifecycle listener. */
154	  once(
155	    event: 'exit' | 'error',
156	    listener: ((code: number | null, signal: NodeJS.Signals | null) => void)
157	      | ((error: Error) => void),
158	  ): void {
159	    this.events.once(event, listener)
160	  }
161	
162	  /** Remove a process lifecycle listener. */
163	  off(
164	    event: 'exit' | 'error',
165	    listener: ((code: number | null, signal: NodeJS.Signals | null) => void)
166	      | ((error: Error) => void),
167	  ): void {
168	    this.events.off(event, listener)
169	  }
170	}

51	 * @returns the harness token accounting, or `undefined` when the product reported none.
52	 */
53	export function bridgeUsage(usage: unknown): TokenUsage | undefined {
54	  if (typeof usage !== 'object' || usage === null) return undefined
55	  const record = usage as Record<string, unknown>
56	  const input = record['input_tokens']
57	  const output = record['output_tokens']
58	  if (typeof input !== 'number' || typeof output !== 'number') return undefined
59	  const cacheRead = record['cache_read_input_tokens']
60	  const cacheWrite = record['cache_creation_input_tokens']
61	  return {
62	    inputTokens: input,
63	    outputTokens: output,
64	    ...typeof cacheRead === 'number' ? { cacheReadTokens: cacheRead } : {},
65	    ...typeof cacheWrite === 'number' ? { cacheWriteTokens: cacheWrite } : {},

77	  if (message.type !== 'assistant') return undefined

79	  const text = blocks

81	    .join('')

194	  const childId = SessionId(randomUUID())
195	  // Captured before the first await: a later parent switch belongs to the
196	  // parent's future, not to this child.
197	  const inherited = captureDelegatedPolicyOverrides(parent)
198	
199	  const handle: AgentHandle = await parent.ctx.agents.create({
200	    sessionId: childId,
201	    meta: childSessionMeta(parent, childDepth, 0),
202	    agentOptions: resolveChildAgentOptions(parent, request.agentOptions, childDepth),
203	    signal: request.signal,
204	    setup: (childCtx: Context): void => {
205	      appendDelegatedPolicyOverrides((childCtx.agent as Agent).session, inherited)

207	      // provider advertises neither capability, so the service has already

209	      applyChildComposition(childCtx, parent, {})
210	      ;(childCtx.agent as Agent).session.append('subagent/descriptor', request.descriptor)
211	    },
212	  })
213	
214	  const agent = handle.agent
215	  let served: McpToolServerHandle
216	  try {
217	    served = toolServer.instance(agent, { serverName: BRIDGE_SERVER_NAME })
218	  } catch (error: unknown) {
219	    await handle.dispose()
220	    throw error
221	  }

223	  const record = bridgeRecorder(agent.session)
224	  record('bridge/start', {
225	    provider,
226	    tools: served.toolNames.map(name => `${BRIDGE_TOOL_PREFIX}${name}`),
227	  })
228	
229	  let settled = false
230	  let lastUsage: TokenUsage | undefined
231	  let released: Promise<void> | undefined
232	  const settle = (stopReason: SubagentStopReason): void => {
233	    if (settled) return
234	    settled = true
235	    record('bridge/end', { stopReason, ...lastUsage === undefined ? {} : { usage: lastUsage } })
236	  }
237	
238	  return {
239	    agent,
240	    id: childId,
241	    options: bridgeQueryOptions(served.config, request.agentOptions?.maxTurns),
242	    observe(message: SDKMessage): void {
243	      if (message.type === 'result') lastUsage = bridgeUsage(message.usage) ?? lastUsage
244	      const assistant = bridgeAssistantRecord(message)
245	      if (assistant !== undefined) record('bridge/assistant', assistant)
246	    },
247	    settle,
248	    release(): Promise<void> {
249	      if (released !== undefined) return released
250	      // The run's record closes before the served turn does, so `bridge/end`
251	      // always lands inside the turn its tool calls occupy.
252	      settle('aborted')

254	      return released
255	    },

2	/**
3	 * Test driver: boot the external-implementer composition, run the
4	 * training-eligible environments once each with the `spawn` subagent provider
5	 * as the implementer, run the same environments again on their own model route,
6	 * and print both fleet reports, the delegation events each delegated cell
7	 * session recorded, the facts of the certified delegated cell, and the
8	 * scoreboard folded from every persisted log, for the e2e's assertions.
9	 */
10	
11	import { boot, resolveConfigPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
12	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
13	import type { EnvironmentDelegation } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner/types'
14	import type { FleetCellOutcome, FleetPlan } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet/types'
15	import type { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
16	
17	const configPath = process.argv[2]
18	if (configPath === undefined) throw new Error('external-implementer driver requires a config path')
19	
20	const ctx = await boot('external-implementer-e2e', resolveConfigPath(configPath, undefined))
21	try {
22	  // Loader siblings mount concurrently; the runner creates agents only over the settled application.
23	  await ctx.get('loader')?.await()
24	  const fleet = ctx.get('fleet')
25	  const scorekeeper = ctx.get('scorekeeper')
26	  const persistence = ctx.get('sessionPersistence')
27	  if (fleet === undefined || scorekeeper === undefined || persistence === undefined) {
28	    throw new Error('external-implementer driver requires the fleet, the scorekeeper, and session persistence')
29	  }
30	  const plan = (group: string, implementer?: FleetPlan['implementer']): FleetPlan => ({
31	    environments: { filter: { heldOut: false } },
32	    models: [],
33	    repetitions: 1,
34	    workspaceRoot: process.cwd(),
35	    group,
36	    ...implementer === undefined ? {} : { implementer },
37	  })
38	  const delegated = await fleet.run(plan('external-implementer-e2e', { kind: 'subagent', provider: 'spawn', label: 'external' }))
39	  const routed = await fleet.run(plan('route-implementer-e2e'))
40	
41	  const sessionOf = (outcome: FleetCellOutcome): SessionId => {
42	    if (!('report' in outcome)) throw new Error(`cell ${outcome.cell.environment} produced no report`)
43	    return outcome.report.sessionId
44	  }
45	  const delegations: Record<string, EnvironmentDelegation[]> = {}
46	  for (const outcome of delegated.cells) {
47	    const { events } = await persistence.inspect(sessionOf(outcome))
48	    delegations[outcome.cell.environment] = events.flatMap(event => (
49	      event.type === 'environment/delegation' ? [event.data] : []
50	    ))
51	  }
52	
53	  const certified = delegated.cells.find(outcome => 'report' in outcome && outcome.report.certified)
54	  if (certified === undefined) throw new Error('external-implementer driver expects one certified delegated cell')
55	  const facts = await scorekeeper.facts(sessionOf(certified))
56	  const scoreboard = await scorekeeper.leaderboard({})
57	  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({
58	    type: 'result',
59	    delegated: { leaderboard: delegated.leaderboard, stamps: delegated.cells.map(outcome => ('report' in outcome ? outcome.report.stamp : null)) },
60	    routed: { leaderboard: routed.leaderboard },
61	    delegations,
62	    facts,
63	    scoreboard,
64	  })}\n`)
65	} finally {
66	  await ctx.fiber.dispose()
67	}

# AGENTS.md — Examples

Runnable harness compositions. `examples/` is one workspace member and the module-resolution root for runnable and test Cordis configs; it is not a build target. [package.json](package.json) declares the packages loaded by those configs, while each leaf's private `package.json` remains metadata only.

Extract reusable logic into `packages/`, where per-file coverage and README gates apply. Examples keep only `cordis.yml` wiring, demo artifacts, and e2e/snapshot scenarios; app package bins own boot glue.

## E2E smokes

Each example has both:

- **Keyless:** boot the real `cordis.yml` through the Loader, drive it, and assert output and clean exit. Catches invalid Loader exports that hand-mounted tests miss ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **With-key:** send a live-model prompt and verify external state, not the model's claim. Self-skip without `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`; see [testing.md](../docs/testing.md).

Keyless process smokes use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke` for Loader launch resolution; terminal tests wrap that launch in a pseudo-terminal. Tests supply paths, environment, input, and assertions. Every checked-in test Cordis config lives under its corresponding `examples/<agent>/` leaf. Map a package-owned config to `examples/<agent>/tests/fixtures/<group>/<package>/cordis.yml`, keep its driver and assertions package-local, and declare every package it names in both root `tsconfig.json` references and `examples/package.json`.

Do not inventory example tests here; the `tests/` trees and root scripts are authoritative.

In `cordis.yml`, comment only non-obvious wiring, load-order consequences, replay, security boundaries, and configuration scope. Do not narrate visible entries; use [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for required coverage and editorial judgment.

See [the root AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for repo-wide conventions and [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) for the design.

=== cordis ===
# The Proving Ground bench: thirty zero-dependency program tasks in three
# domains, registered from their task.json files, run on the operator's Claude
# Code subscription through the harness's own agent loop (the LLM route) or
# through the product's own loop (the external implementer), and compared in
# frozen paired experiments. No cadence: the drivers beside this file run one
# plan each.
#
# The route serves three product models under one provider. Every arm of an
# experiment names one of them, so a comparison between models and a comparison
# between implementers both read from the same catalog. The product envelope
# around each query is the one model-visible input the log does not hold.
- id: llm-claude-code
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-claude-code'
  config:
    provider: claude-code
    models:
      - id: opus
        name: Claude Code opus
        productModel: opus
        contextWindow: 200000
      - id: sonnet
        name: Claude Code sonnet
        productModel: sonnet
        contextWindow: 200000
      - id: haiku
        name: Claude Code haiku
        productModel: haiku
        contextWindow: 200000
    effort: medium
    queryTimeoutMs: 300000

# Managed child-process groups for the bash executor, for the CLI the route
# spawns per query, and for the product the external implementer spawns.
- id: subprocess
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local'

- id: bash
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-local'

# The filesystem tools resolve paths against the cell session's cwd, which the
# runner sets to the cell workspace; the policy loads first so writes and edits
# require an observed file.
- id: fs-local
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-local'

- id: fs-observation-policy
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-observation-policy'

- id: tool-fs
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'

- id: goal
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'
  config:
    defaultMaxGoalRounds: 11

- id: verification
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
  config:
    maxChecks: 32
    maxTextChars: 4096

- id: environments
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'

- id: register-environments
  name: './register-environments.ts'

# The default route of a cell agent; an experiment arm or a fleet plan names the
# model explicitly, so this only decides what an unnamed request runs.
- id: agent-default-model
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
  config:
    provider: claude-code
    model: sonnet

- id: subagents
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'

# The product's own loop as an implementer, for the arm that measures it
# against the harness loop: unattended edits and the test command allowed,
# nothing else. Its spend is outside every limit this harness enforces.
- id: subagent-claude-code
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-claude-code'
  config:
    permissionMode: acceptEdits
    allowedTools:
      - 'Bash(node:*)'

# `isolation: none` is the only claim the external arm can serve; both arms run
# under the same claim so the certificates compare.
- id: environment-runner
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner'
  config:
    isolation: none
    maxAttempts: 3
    evidenceMaxChars: 2048

- id: fleet
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet'
  config:
    maxConcurrent: 2
    workspaceRetention: keep

- id: experiments
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments'
  config:
    bootstrapResamples: 2000
    confidenceLevel: 0.95
    minimumDelta: 0.05
    cellTokenCap: 600000
    tokenBudget: 200000000

# Village rule: unattended cells carry a session budget. A cell that has not
# certified within these caps is a failed cell, not a longer one.
- id: budget-policy
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy'
  config:
    maxTotalTokens: 1500000
    maxWallMs: 1200000

- id: agent-spine
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-spine-demo'
  config:
    persona: |
      You implement one program task in the workspace you are given, against its own test suite, and you stop when the tests pass.

      The workspace is your working directory: every bash command and every file path resolves inside it, so read and edit its files by their relative paths and never search outside it.
    workspaceContext: false

- id: persistence
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl'
  config:
    root: './.sessions'
    compression: none

- id: checkpoint-policy
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-checkpoint-policy'

# Evaluation terms only: bench sessions never train.
- id: data-use
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-data-use'
  config:
    clientId: daliesk-lab
    agreementId: proving-ground-bench
    purposes:
      - evaluation
    residency: eu-west
    retentionDays: 90
    redactionProfile: village-v1

- id: session-projection
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-projection'

- id: scorekeeper
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper'

    passAtK:

1	/**
2	 * Provider-side vocabulary for OUT-OF-PROCESS subagent backends — the pieces
3	 * that enforce this seam's own contracts around a child in another process:
4	 * the no-capabilities advertisement, timing-bound validation, child
5	 * working-directory resolution (config override, else the delegating parent
6	 * session's workspace), the never-reject result settlement, and the standard
7	 * run-handle publication. Backends compose these with their own wire drivers;
8	 * the process machinery itself (spawn, env scrub, tree-scoped teardown)
9	 * belongs to the `dsh-subprocess` seam.
10	 *
11	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent/out-of-process
12	 */
13	
14	import { accessSync, constants, statSync } from 'node:fs'
15	import { isAbsolute, resolve } from 'node:path'
16	import type { ContentBlock } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
17	import type { SubagentCapabilities, SubagentResult, SubagentRun, SubagentStopReason } from './types.ts'
18	
19	/**
20	 * The capability advertisement of an out-of-process backend: NONE. A child in
21	 * another process cannot honor parent-enforced start features
22	 * (`outputSchema`/`maxDepth`/`toolFilter`/`persona`/`harnessTools`), so the
23	 * service rejects a request needing any of them before `start` runs — never
24	 * accepted-then-ignored. A backend that bridges the harness tool set into the
25	 * foreign model declares `harnessTools` itself instead of taking this
26	 * advertisement.
27	 */
28	export const NO_START_CAPABILITIES: SubagentCapabilities = Object.freeze({
29	  outputSchema: false,
30	  depthLimit: false,
31	  toolFilter: false,
32	  persona: false,
33	  harnessTools: false,
34	})
35	
36	/**
37	 * Whether a provider's advertisement is the out-of-process one. A caller that
38	 * must know where a NAMED provider runs its child asks here instead of matching
39	 * provider names: the four parent-enforced start-time features
40	 * (`outputSchema`, `depthLimit`, `toolFilter`, `persona`) can only be honored
41	 * by a driver that composes the child in this process, so an in-process driver
42	 * supports at least one of them and a backend that launches a foreign agent
43	 * supports none. `harnessTools` is deliberately not read: a bridging backend
44	 * advertises it while its child still runs in another process, because the
45	 * served tools execute here and the model does not. The test fails closed,
46	 * which is what a caller needs it for: an unknown backend that advertises
47	 * nothing is treated as one this process cannot fence.
48	 * @param capabilities - the provider's {@link SubagentCapabilities} advertisement.
49	 * @returns true when the provider advertises no parent-enforced start-time capability.
50	 */
51	export function runsOutOfProcess(capabilities: SubagentCapabilities): boolean {
52	  const { outputSchema, depthLimit, toolFilter, persona } = capabilities
53	  return !outputSchema && !depthLimit && !toolFilter && !persona
54	}
55	
56	/**
57	 * Assert a configured timing bound is a positive finite number (it bounds a
58	 * teardown or shutdown wait; zero, negative, or NaN would skip or wedge it).
59	 * @param prefix - the consuming plugin's diagnostic prefix (e.g. `subagent-acp`).
60	 * @param name - the config field name, for the diagnostic.
61	 * @param value - the configured value.
62	 */
63	export function assertPositiveFinite(prefix: string, name: string, value: number): void {
64	  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value <= 0) {
65	    throw new Error(`${prefix}: ${name} must be a positive finite number`)
66	  }
67	}
68	
69	/**
70	 * Whether `path` names an existing directory the harness can ENTER. The
71	 * search-permission probe matters: `statSync().isDirectory()` is true for a
72	 * mode-600 directory, but a subprocess cwd needs `X_OK` or spawn fails EACCES.
73	 */
74	function isEnterableDirectory(path: string): boolean {
75	  try {
76	    if (!statSync(path).isDirectory()) return false
77	    accessSync(path, constants.X_OK)
78	    return true
79	  } catch {
80	    // statSync/accessSync throw only filesystem access errors here
81	    // (ENOENT/EACCES/ENOTDIR/…), and every one of them means the path cannot
82	    // serve as the child's cwd.
83	    return false
84	  }
85	}
86	
87	/**
88	 * Assert `cwd` can actually host the child: absolute (it doubles as the
89	 * child's workspace identity, and a relative path would be re-anchored to the
90	 * server process's launch directory) and an existing directory (fail here,
91	 * before the process boundary, instead of as an ambiguous spawn ENOENT).
92	 * @param prefix - the consuming plugin's diagnostic prefix.
93	 * @param label - which source supplied the value, for the diagnostic.
94	 * @param cwd - the candidate working directory.
95	 * @returns `cwd`, validated.
96	 */
97	export function assertUsableCwd(prefix: string, label: string, cwd: string): string {
98	  if (!isAbsolute(cwd)) {
99	    throw new Error(`${prefix}: ${label} must be an absolute path: ${cwd}`)
100	  }
101	  if (!isEnterableDirectory(cwd)) {
102	    throw new Error(`${prefix}: ${label} is not an accessible directory: ${cwd}`)
103	  }
104	  return cwd
105	}
106	
107	/**
108	 * Validate a configured `cwd` override ONCE, at plugin load: reject the empty
109	 * string (`path.resolve('')` is the process cwd — it would silently
110	 * reintroduce the launch-directory fallback this resolution removes),
111	 * interpret a relative path against the harness launch directory, and require
112	 * an enterable directory.
113	 * @param prefix - the consuming plugin's diagnostic prefix.
114	 * @param cwd - the configured override, or `undefined` when the config omits it.
115	 * @returns the validated absolute override, or `undefined` when omitted.
116	 */
117	export function validateConfiguredCwd(prefix: string, cwd: string | undefined): string | undefined {
118	  if (cwd === undefined) return undefined
119	  if (cwd === '') {
120	    throw new Error(`${prefix}: config cwd must not be empty — omit the key to inherit the parent session cwd`)
121	  }
122	  return assertUsableCwd(prefix, 'config cwd', resolve(cwd))
123	}
124	
125	/**
126	 * Resolve the child's working directory at start: the deployment override
127	 * when configured (already validated at load), else the parent session's
128	 * workspace cwd (validated here, its earliest resolvable point). Fails loud
129	 * when neither exists — falling back to the harness process cwd would
130	 * silently bind the child to the server's launch directory instead of the
131	 * delegating session's workspace (one server process serves many sessions,
132	 * each with its own cwd).
133	 * @param prefix - the consuming plugin's diagnostic prefix.
134	 * @param configured - the load-validated override, or `undefined`.
135	 * @param parentCwd - the delegating parent session's workspace cwd, if any.
136	 * @returns the absolute child working directory.
137	 */
138	export function resolveChildCwd(prefix: string, configured: string | undefined, parentCwd: string | undefined): string {
139	  if (configured !== undefined) return configured
140	  if (parentCwd === undefined) {
141	    throw new Error(`${prefix}: no working directory for the child — configure \`cwd\` or delegate from a parent session that has one`)
142	  }
143	  return assertUsableCwd(prefix, 'parent session cwd', parentCwd)
144	}
145	
146	/** Normalize an unknown thrown value to an Error (the catch binding is `unknown`). */
147	function toError(value: unknown): Error {
148	  // The rejecting surfaces (wire clients, spawn failures) only throw
149	  // `Error`s; the `String(value)` arm is a defensive fallback for a non-Error
150	  // throw the typed surfaces cannot produce.
151	  /* v8 ignore next */
152	  return value instanceof Error ? value : new Error(String(value))
153	}
154	
155	/** Inputs to {@link settleRunResult}. */
156	export interface RunResultSettlement {
157	  /** The turn attempt (typically racing local cancellation); returns the terminal result. */
158	  attempt: () => Promise<SubagentResult>
159	  /** Snapshot the provider exposes when cancellation or failure wins settlement. */
160	  collectOutput: () => ContentBlock[]
161	  /** Whether local cancellation settled before the attempt's outcome is observed. */
162	  cancelled: () => boolean
163	  /** Diagnostic sink for a failure flattened to a stop reason; a throw from it is contained. */
164	  onError?: ((error: Error, stopReason: SubagentStopReason) => void) | undefined
165	  /** The request's cancellation signal (the listener is removed at settlement). */
166	  signal: AbortSignal
167	  /** The abort listener registered on {@link signal} at start. */
168	  onAbort: () => void
169	}
170	
171	/**
172	 * Settle an out-of-process run result under the seam contract: `result` never
173	 * rejects after publication. A normally completed or rejected attempt resolves
174	 * as `aborted` when cancellation already settled locally; another rejection is
175	 * flattened to `stopReason: 'error'` through the contained diagnostic sink.
176	 * The abort listener is removed on every path.
177	 * @param parts - the attempt, output snapshot, cancellation state, sink, and signal wiring.
178	 * @returns the terminal result (never a rejection).
179	 */
180	export async function settleRunResult(parts: RunResultSettlement): Promise<SubagentResult> {
181	  try {
182	    const result = await parts.attempt()
183	    return parts.cancelled()
184	      ? { output: parts.collectOutput(), stopReason: 'aborted' }
185	      : result
186	  } catch (error: unknown) {
187	    // Cover a rejection already queued when cancellation arrives.
188	    if (parts.cancelled()) return { output: parts.collectOutput(), stopReason: 'aborted' }
189	    // Flatten post-publication transport failures while preserving diagnostics.
190	    try {
191	      parts.onError?.(toError(error), 'error')
192	    } catch {
193	      // The diagnostic sink cannot reject the run result.
194	    }
195	    return { output: parts.collectOutput(), stopReason: 'error' }
196	  } finally {
197	    parts.signal.removeEventListener('abort', parts.onAbort)
198	  }
199	}
200	
201	/** Inputs to {@link subprocessRunHandle}. */
202	export interface SubprocessRunHandleParts {
203	  /** The parent-scoped run id. */
204	  id: SubagentRun['id']
205	  /**
206	   * The published in-process child a bridging backend created to authorize the
207	   * foreign agent's tool calls, or absent when the child exists only in the
208	   * other process. Its id MUST be {@link id}.
209	   */
210	  localAgent?: SubagentRun['localAgent']
211	  /** The flattened, never-rejecting result (the seam contract). */
212	  result: Promise<SubagentResult>
213	  /** The request's cancellation signal (the listener is removed on dispose). */
214	  signal: AbortSignal
215	  /** The abort listener registered on {@link signal} at start. */
216	  onAbort: () => void
217	  /** Settle local cancellation so {@link result} resolves without the child. */
218	  requestCancel: () => void
219	  /** Tear the child process down to quiescence (backend-owned ladder). */
220	  teardown: () => Promise<void>
221	}
222	
223	/**
224	 * Publish the seam run handle for an out-of-process child. `dispose()` is
225	 * idempotent (one memoized teardown): it removes the abort listener, settles
226	 * local cancellation — there is no assumption the child cooperates — and then
227	 * awaits the backend's teardown to actual exit.
228	 * @param parts - the run identity, result, cancellation wiring, and teardown.
229	 * @returns the seam run handle (`localAgent` is `undefined` unless the backend published one).
230	 */
231	export function subprocessRunHandle(parts: SubprocessRunHandleParts): SubagentRun {
232	  let disposal: Promise<void> | undefined
233	  return {
234	    id: parts.id,
235	    localAgent: parts.localAgent,
236	    result: parts.result,
237	    dispose(): Promise<void> {
238	      if (disposal !== undefined) return disposal
239	      parts.signal.removeEventListener('abort', parts.onAbort)
240	      parts.requestCancel()
241	      disposal = parts.teardown()
242	      return disposal
243	    },
244	  }
245	}

2	 * Fixed Codex one-shot subagent provider. Every accepted run starts a fresh
3	 * official `codex app-server --stdio` process in the delegating Session's
4	 * workspace and publishes only after an ephemeral thread exists.
5	 *
6	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-codex
7	 */
8	
9	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
10	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
11	import { MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-timeout'
12	import {
13	  assertOutOfProcessAllowed,
14	  assertPositiveFinite,
15	  enforceOutOfProcessRefusal,
16	  NO_START_CAPABILITIES,
17	  resolveChildCwd,
18	  type ResolvedSubagentStartRequest,
19	  type SubagentCapabilities,
20	  type SubagentProvider,
21	} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'
22	import {
23	  DEFAULT_DISPOSE_GRACE_MS,
24	  startCodexRun,
25	  type CodexRunSpec,
26	} from './run.ts'
27	
28	export const name = 'subagent-codex'
29	export const inject = ['subagents', 'subprocess']
30	
31	/** Deployment-owned environment and process-release bound. */
32	export interface Config {
33	  /**
34	   * Explicit environment entries layered over the subprocess seam's
35	   * credential-scrubbed parent environment.
36	   */
37	  env?: Record<string, string>
38	  /** Grace in milliseconds for app-server process-tree termination. */
39	  disposeGraceMs?: number
40	}
41	
42	export const Config: z<Config> = z.object({
43	  env: z.dict(z.string()).default({}),
44	  disposeGraceMs: z.number().default(DEFAULT_DISPOSE_GRACE_MS),
45	})
46	
47	type ResolvedConfig = Required<Config>
48	
49	class CodexProvider implements SubagentProvider {
50	  readonly name = 'codex'
51	  readonly capabilities: SubagentCapabilities = NO_START_CAPABILITIES
52	  readonly inheritsParentContext = false
53	
54	  constructor(
55	    private readonly ctx: Context,
56	    private readonly config: ResolvedConfig,
57	  ) {}
58	
59	  start(request: ResolvedSubagentStartRequest) {
60	    assertOutOfProcessAllowed(this.ctx, request.parent)
61	    const parentCwd = request.parent.session.header.cwd
62	    if (parentCwd === undefined) {
63	      throw new Error(
64	        'subagent-codex: no working directory for the child — delegate from a parent session that has one',
65	      )
66	    }
67	    const spec: CodexRunSpec = {
68	      cwd: resolveChildCwd(
69	        'subagent-codex',
70	        undefined,
71	        parentCwd,
72	      ),
73	      env: this.config.env,
74	      disposeGraceMs: this.config.disposeGraceMs,
75	      spawn: spawnSpec => this.ctx.subprocess.spawn(spawnSpec),
76	      onError: (error, stopReason) => {
77	        this.ctx.logger.warn(
78	          `subagent-codex: child run failed (${stopReason}): ${error.message}`,
79	        )
80	      },
81	    }
82	    return startCodexRun(request, spec)
83	  }
84	}

86	/**
87	 * Register the fixed `codex` provider.
88	 * @param ctx - context carrying shared subagent and subprocess services.
89	 * @param config - explicit child environment and disposal grace.
90	 */
91	export function apply(ctx: Context, config: Config): void {
92	  const resolved = config as ResolvedConfig
93	  assertPositiveFinite(
94	    'subagent-codex',
95	    'disposeGraceMs',
96	    resolved.disposeGraceMs,
97	  )
98	  if (resolved.disposeGraceMs > MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS) {
99	    throw new Error(
100	      `subagent-codex: disposeGraceMs must be no greater than ${MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS}`,

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-claude-code
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	This package registers the fixed `claude-code` subagent provider. Each accepted run invokes the official Claude Agent SDK in the delegating Session's workspace, resolves the native `claude` executable through the shared subprocess service, submits one self-contained text task, and returns only the final answer through the shared [`dsh-subagent`](../subagent/README.md) result contract.
6	
7	## Start and ownership
8	
9	`start(request)` accepts only a non-empty sequence of text blocks and derives the child cwd from the parent Session. It creates one private `AbortController`, calls the official SDK `query()`, and publishes the run only after the SDK's `spawnClaudeCodeProcess` hook has supplied a live CLI handle owned by [`dsh-subprocess`](../../subprocess/subprocess/README.md). A failure or cancellation before publication closes the query, terminates any acquired process tree, waits for it to exit, and rejects `start()`.
10	
11	The SDK receives the exact concatenated text task. The provider iterates the complete SDK message stream and accepts only a `result` message with `subtype: "success"`, `is_error: false`, and a nonblank `result`, followed by normal iterator completion. Every SDK error subtype, an error-marked success, a missing answer, iterator failure, protocol failure, or process failure maps to `error`; the provider produces neither `max-tokens` nor `refusal`.
12	
13	Local cancellation wins the result race and maps to `aborted`. `dispose()` is idempotent: it aborts the run, asks the SDK query to close, invokes the shared process-tree termination escalation, and waits for whole-tree exit. SDK graceful close expresses protocol intent; the subprocess handle remains the authority for process quiescence. Result failure and independent teardown failure remain separate.
14	
15	Before anything is spawned, `start()` asks the composed [read barrier](../../verification/read-barrier/README.md) whether this out-of-process child may run at all. An implementer session under a deployment claiming `process` or `host` isolation is refused with `SubagentError` `READ_BARRIER_REFUSED`, because a foreign agent brings its own tool stack and no fence this process installs reaches its reads; under a claim of `none` nothing is refused. The provider registers that refusal with the barrier, so the scope census reports `subagent`.
16	
17	The refusal applies to both modes, bridge mode included. Bridge mode is what makes relaxing it conceivable — under it every read the external model performs is a harness tool call through this process's executor, where the barrier already denies — but it is not sufficient: the CLI process itself is unconfined, so it can open a denied path with its own runtime rather than through an MCP call. Confining that process is separate work against the sandbox seam.
18	
19	## Native settings and interaction
20	
21	Outside bridge mode the provider deliberately omits the SDK `settingSources` option. The official SDK therefore reads the host's normal user, project, and local Claude settings relative to the parent Session cwd, including native account state and product configuration. The provider neither copies nor filters those files and does not create or modify login state. Bridge mode passes `settingSources: []` instead, because a workspace setting that added a tool or a hook would reopen the surface bridge mode exists to close; authentication is unaffected, since the SDK resolves the account independently of that option.
22	
23	Each query sets `persistSession: false` and disables `AskUserQuestion`. It supplies no elicitation or dialog callback, so unattended interactions fail through the SDK instead of waiting for a user interface this provider does not own. The only `canUseTool` the provider ever supplies is bridge mode's own tool fence, which asks nobody anything: it decides from the tool name alone.
24	
25	## Bridge mode: the harness tool set, and nothing else
26	
27	A request carrying `harnessTools: { only: true }` runs the same product against a completely different tool surface. The provider creates a child harness agent under the parent's lineage — the parent's cwd, its preset composition, its delegated sandbox and approval policy, the resolved delegation depth — serves that agent's tool registry through [`dsh-mcp-tool-server`](../../mcp/mcp-tool-server/README.md) as the SDK server named `dsh`, and pins the external model to it:
28	
29	| SDK option | Value | Why |
30	|---|---|---|
31	| `tools` | `[]` | No built-in tool of the product's own. |
32	| `mcpServers` | `{ dsh: <in-process instance> }` | The harness registry, in this process. |
33	| `allowedTools` | `['mcp__dsh__*']` | Harness tools run without a product-side permission prompt. |
34	| `canUseTool` | denies every name outside `mcp__dsh__` | The fence. `allowedTools` decides what is auto-approved, not what may be called. |
35	| `strictMcpConfig` | `true` | No MCP server from the workspace, user settings, or plugins. |
36	| `settingSources` | `[]` | No project settings, hooks, CLAUDE.md, or agent frontmatter. |
37	| `maxTurns` | `agentOptions.maxTurns` when set | The caller's turn ceiling reaches the external loop. |
38	
39	Every tool call the external model makes is therefore an ordinary harness execution on the child agent: authorized by the approval seam, filtered by the registry guards, bounded by the tool-call timeout, and recorded as the usual `tool/call`/`tool/result` pair. The final answer still returns through the shared result contract, and `SubagentRun.localAgent` is the published child, whose id is the run id.
40	
41	The pinned SDK warns that a bare `allowedTools` entry auto-approves before `canUseTool` runs. That is the intended split: the served harness tools need no product-side prompt, while every other name falls through to the callback and is denied there.
42	
43	### What the child session records
44	
45	`src/types.ts` declares three log-only events, none of which enters any harness model's context:
46	
47	| Event | Payload | When |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| `bridge/start` | `provider`, `tools` (the names as the external model sees them) | Once, after the server is attached. |
50	| `bridge/assistant` | `text`, optional `usage` | Per assistant message with text. Tool calls are absent: the executor already logged each as the durable pair. |
51	| `bridge/end` | `stopReason`, optional `usage` | Once, when the run settles or is released. |
52	
53	The whole run is one turn of that child session, because the durable tool pair is step-scoped; [`dsh-mcp-tool-server`](../../mcp/mcp-tool-server/README.md) owns that turn and closes it on disposal.
54	
55	The log does NOT hold the external model's hidden reasoning, its assembled system prompt, or its own context: none of it is observable from this process. A reader of the child log sees what the external agent said and did, never why.
56	
57	## Capabilities and context
58	
59	The provider advertises `harnessTools` and no other optional start-time capability, and reports `inheritsParentContext: false`. `harnessTools` is the one start-time feature an out-of-process child can honor, because the harness composes the child agent whose tools it serves rather than asking the product to enforce anything. `outputSchema`, `maxDepth`, `toolFilter`, and `persona` are still rejected by the shared service for this provider, in both modes.
60	
61	Without `harnessTools`, Claude Code receives the standalone text task and the parent Session cwd, but not the parent conversation, persona, tool filter, depth policy, or structured-output contract. Every run has an independent SDK query, cancellation controller, CLI process, and non-persisted product session.
62	
63	## Configuration
64	
65	| Key | Default | Meaning |
66	|---|---|---|
67	| `env` | `{}` | Explicit SDK/CLI environment layered over the shared credential-scrubbed parent environment. |
68	| `disposeGraceMs` | `3000` | Positive finite grace in milliseconds, no greater than [`MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS`](../../util/timeout/README.md), between the shared process-tree owner's termination tiers; disposal then waits for whole-tree exit. |
69	| `permissionMode` | absent | The product's own permission mode for both modes, one of the pinned SDK's values (`default`, `acceptEdits`, `bypassPermissions`, `plan`, `dontAsk`, `auto`); any other value is refused at load. Absent leaves the product's default. |
70	| `allowedTools` | `[]` | Tool names the product auto-approves in the BLACK-BOX mode only; empty leaves the product's default. Bridge mode ignores it and keeps its own allowlist and denial callback. |
71	
72	Under the host's native settings the product's default permission mode prompts before a file write, so an unattended black-box child reports that it lacks permission rather than doing the work. An unattended implementer at `isolation: none` therefore needs `acceptEdits` (file edits) or `bypassPermissions` (everything, and the provider pairs it with the SDK's required `allowDangerouslySkipPermissions`). Both hand the product's own confinement away — which is exactly what bridge mode replaces: there the harness authorizes each call at its own executor, so no product-side permission decision is involved at all.
73	
74	Production resolves `claude` from the subprocess execution world's credential-scrubbed `PATH`, with explicit `env` entries applied, and passes the resulting path to the SDK as `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable`. On Windows, a resolved `.cmd` or `.bat` path is carried as a quoted, per-spawn environment value that `cmd.exe /v:off` expands once, so valid path metacharacters remain data. The pinned SDK's fixed flags then occupy cmd's command tail and contain no cmd metacharacters; they are not ordinary Windows argv. Native settings and authentication remain authoritative. The plugin does not install another CLI, select a model, create a product home, log in, or probe an account. Credential-shaped ambient variables are removed before the explicit `env` overlay is applied, so an API key or token intended for the child must be supplied there. Non-credential endpoint variables such as `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, along with ordinary ambient values such as `PATH` and `HOME`, remain inherited unless overridden.
75	
76	Shipped profiles load this provider once on the host and start no Claude process until a tool call. Full Agent Presets carry the tool row below with `disabled: true`; copy a preset and remove that field to expose `subagent_claude_code` only to agents composed from the copy. A custom host composition can still use both rows directly.
77	
78	```yaml
79	- id: subagent-claude-code
80	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-claude-code'
81	  config:
82	    env:
83	      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: !!js process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
84	
85	- id: tool-subagent-claude-code
86	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
87	  disabled: true
88	  config:
89	    provider: claude-code
90	    toolName: subagent_claude_code
91	    enableRunInBackground: false
92	    maxDepth: provider-managed
93	```
94	
95	## Product compatibility and evidence
96	
97	The runtime dependency is pinned to `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.220`. Production runs the native `claude` installation. The keyless real-product test uses the SDK-distributed Claude Code 2.1.220 CLI as a deterministic fixture, routed through the same native executable-resolution and Windows batch-shim path; it does not claim compatibility with every independently installed version. Loader composition proves that both product packages coexist without starting either product.
98	
99	The project owner's identity-scoped distribution authorization covers the official SDK and the official CLI/platform payloads declared by each SDK version. [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](../../../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) discloses the current optional payload closure without classifying its declared terms as permissive; unrelated non-permissive runtime dependencies continue to fail the notices gate.
100	
101	## Model Experience
102	
103	### Child request
104	
105	#### What the model sees
106	
107	The Claude Code child receives the standalone text task as one fresh SDK query. Its workspace is the parent Session cwd, while its model, system instructions, tools, permissions, and authentication come from the host's native Claude settings and product installation. Under `harnessTools: { only: true }` the tools instead come from the child harness agent's registry, and the host's settings, hooks, project files, and MCP servers are excluded — only the model and the authentication remain the product's.
108	
109	#### Token effect
110	
111	The child pays for an independent Claude Code context and query. Child tokens do not enter the parent's context.
112	
113	#### KV Cache effect
114	
115	Independent of the parent request cache. Reuse depends only on Claude Code's own model, instructions, tools, native settings, and fresh query.
116	
117	### Parent tool result, indirectly
118	
119	#### What the model sees
120	
121	Through `dsh-tool-subagent`, the parent sees only the strict final Claude Code answer or the consumer's exact error for a non-completed result. Claude Code reasoning, tool activity, intermediate messages, stderr, workspace diffs, usage, and product ids are not copied into the parent Session.
122	
123	#### Token effect
124	
125	Parent input grows only by the final answer or error retained in the tool result. This provider adds no parent tool schema by itself.
126	
127	#### KV Cache effect
128	
129	Append-only: the new tool result follows the reusable parent request prefix.
130	
131	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
132	
133	- **One fresh query and process per run** — there is no continuation, resume, pooling, progress stream, or product-session persistence.
134	- **Host settings are intentionally authoritative** — project and user settings can change model, tools, and behavior; the provider does not provide a filtered or hermetic production mode.
135	- **Product installation and account state remain native** — a missing or incompatible `claude`, configuration error, or authentication failure is surfaced as a startup or run error; the plugin provides no installer or login flow.
136	- **The SDK platform CLI remains in the install closure** — production ignores it in favor of the host `claude`, but the current SDK optional dependency is still installed and supplies the keyless compatibility fixture. Removing that payload belongs to the separate product installation-closure follow-up.
137	- **No human interaction path** — `AskUserQuestion` is disabled and other interactive callbacks are absent, so tasks requiring new approval or input fail instead of suspending.
138	- **Final text only outside bridge mode** — without `harnessTools`, reasoning, intermediate messages, tool traffic, usage, stderr, and workspace diffs remain product-local. Bridge mode records the tool traffic, the assistant text, and the usage; the reasoning and the product's own prompt stay unobservable in both.
139	- **No optional shared capabilities besides `harnessTools`** — output schemas, child personas, tool filtering, and harness depth enforcement are rejected by the shared service for this provider. `toolFilter` is meaningful in bridge mode and refused there too: capability flags are per provider rather than per mode, so advertising it would accept it in the black-box mode as well, where it would be silently ignored.
140	- **Bridge mode needs the tool server composed** — a deployment that requests `harnessTools` without [`dsh-mcp-tool-server`](../../mcp/mcp-tool-server/README.md) is refused at start with `SubagentError` `BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE`, because the provider cannot serve a registry that is not there.
141	- **The bridged process is unconfined** — bridge mode fences the tools the external model is given, not the process it runs in.
142	- **No wall-clock timeout or side-effect rollback** — the caller cancels long work, and files or external systems changed before cancellation are not restored.
143

94	 * and disposal work through the returned run. Rejection means the agent
95	 * factory's unpublished creation transaction reached quiescence without
96	 * publishing a child. Every start appends its resolved descriptor inside the
97	 * child's initial turn.

99	 * @param options - the optional fork seed.

102	export async function startInProcessRun(
103	  request: ResolvedSubagentStartRequest,
104	  options: InProcessRunOptions,
105	): Promise<SubagentRun> {

107	  if (request.signal.aborted) throw prePublicationAbort()

109	  const childDepth = resolveChildDepth(parent, request.maxDepth)

112	  const seed = options.seed
113	  const activationBoundary = seed?.length ?? 0

115	  // Capture before the first await: a later parent switch belongs to the
116	  // parent's future.
117	  const inherited = captureDelegatedPolicyOverrides(parent)
118

125	    })

128	    }

130	  }

132	  const handle = await parent.ctx.agents.create({
133	    sessionId: childId,
134	    meta: childSessionMeta(parent, childDepth, activationBoundary),
135	    ...seed !== undefined ? { seed } : {},
136	    agentOptions: resolveChildAgentOptions(parent, request.agentOptions, childDepth),
137	    signal: request.signal,
138	    setup,
139	  })

141	    handle,

150	/**
151	 * Wrap a published child in the single run lifecycle that owns signal handoff,
152	 * one turn, result settlement, and quiescent disposal.
153	 */
154	function drivePublishedRun(
155	  handle: AgentHandle,
156	  signal: AbortSignal,
157	  prompt: ContentBlock[],
158	  childId: SessionId,
159	  boundary: number,
160	  structured: StructuredAttachment | undefined,
161	): SubagentRun {
162	  const child = handle.agent
163	  const flags = { cancelled: false }
164	  const onAbort = (): void => {
165	    flags.cancelled = true
166	    child.cancel({ kind: 'parent' })
167	  }
168	  signal.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true })
169	  // Agent creation detaches its creation-only listener before returning. The
170	  // post-registration check closes that handoff without treating an already
171	  // published child as a failed start.
172	  if (signal.aborted) onAbort()
173	
174	  const result: Promise<SubagentResult> = (async () => {
175	    try {
176	      if (!flags.cancelled) {
177	        child.followup(createUserMessage({ content: prompt, source: { kind: 'user' } }))
178	        await child.whenIdle()
179	      }
180	      return readResult(
181	        child,
182	        boundary,
183	        flags.cancelled,
184	        structured ? { captured: structured.captured() } : undefined,
185	      )
186	    } finally {
187	      signal.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort)
188	    }
189	  })()
190	
191	  return {
192	    id: childId,
193	    localAgent: child,
194	    result,
195	    async dispose(): Promise<void> {
196	      signal.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort)
197	      flags.cancelled = true
198	      const settlements = await Promise.allSettled([handle.dispose(), result])
199	      const disposal = settlements[0]
200	      // The result channel owns run faults; disposal reports only failure to
201	      // release the published handle after both operations settle.
202	      if (disposal.status === 'rejected') throw disposal.reason
203	    },
204	  }
205	}
206	
207	/** Read one settled child's result from events after its activation boundary. */
208	function readResult(
209	  child: Agent,
210	  boundary: number,
211	  cancelled: boolean,
212	  structured?: { captured?: { value: unknown } | undefined },
213	): SubagentResult {
214	  const own = child.session.events.slice(boundary)
215	  // `droppedUnrun` is deliberately unread: a one-shot prompt is claimed by its
216	  // awaited first turn almost immediately, and the owner's own teardown is the
217	  // `cancelled` flag below. A cancellation with no accounting turn resolves
218	  // `error` through `toStopReason(undefined)`, which never overstates success.
219	  const lastEnd = foldConsumedWork(own).end
220	  // The seam's canonical selection rule; a partial answer survives cancel and truncation.
221	  const output: ContentBlock[] = finalAssistantOutput(own) ?? []
222	  const recorded = toStopReason(lastEnd?.data.reason)
223	  // Disposal can tear the owner down before the loop records its ordinary
224	  // `aborted` end, yielding `disposed` instead.
225	  const stopReason: SubagentStopReason = cancelled && recorded !== 'completed' ? 'aborted' : recorded
226	  if (structured !== undefined) {
227	    if (structured.captured !== undefined) {
228	      return { output, structured: structured.captured.value, stopReason }
229	    }
230	    if (stopReason === 'completed') return { output, stopReason: cancelled ? 'aborted' : 'error' }
231	  }
232	  return { output, stopReason }
233	}

9:`start(request)` accepts only a non-empty sequence of text blocks and derives the child cwd from the parent Session. It then spawns the fixed command through [`dsh-subprocess`](../../subprocess/subprocess/README.md), performs `initialize` → `initialized` → `thread/start { cwd, ephemeral: true }`, and publishes the run only after Codex returns a valid ephemeral thread. A failure or cancellation before publication closes the wire, terminates the managed process tree, waits for it to exit, and rejects `start()`.
30:Production resolves `codex` from `PATH` and uses the host's native Codex configuration and authentication. The plugin does not install Codex, select a model, create `CODEX_HOME`, log in, or probe a version. Credential-shaped ambient variables are removed by the subprocess seam, so an API key intended for the child must be supplied explicitly in `env`; ordinary ambient values such as `PATH` and `HOME` remain available unless overridden.
55:## Model Experience
59:#### What the model sees
61:The Codex child receives the standalone text blocks as one turn in a fresh ephemeral thread. Its workspace is the parent Session cwd, and its model, system instructions, tools, sandbox, and authentication come from the native Codex installation and configuration.
69:Independent of the parent request cache. Reuse depends only on Codex's own provider, model, instructions, tools, and ephemeral-thread request.
73:#### What the model sees
88:- **Host-managed product installation and account state** — a missing or incompatible `codex`, configuration error, or authentication failure is surfaced as a startup or run error; the plugin provides no installer, login flow, or runtime version gate.
89:- **Compatibility is pinned by development evidence** — upgrading from the verified 0.147.0 protocol baseline requires regenerating upstream schema evidence and rerunning handshake, answer-selection, approval, cancellation, keyless real-product, and credentialed DeepSeek nonce tests.

        if 'harnessTools:' not in line:

        m = re.match(r'^(\s*)harnessTools: (true|false),\s*$', line)

            continue
        line2 = re.sub(r'(harnessTools: (?:true|false))(\s*\})', r'\1, model: false\2', line)
        if line2 != line:
            result[-1] = line2
            continue
    new = '\n'.join(result)
    if new != text:
        p.write_text(new)
        changed.append(rel)
print('\n'.join(changed))

 * terminal `result` message. Same process boundary as the usage beside it: a
 * value that is not a number yields none rather than a fabricated zero.
 * @param message - one message from the SDK stream.
 * @returns the product's own US-dollar total, or `undefined` for every other message.
 */
export function resultReportedCostUsd(message: SDKMessage): number | undefined {
  if (message.type !== 'result') return undefined
  const cost: unknown = message.total_cost_usd
  return typeof cost === 'number' ? cost : undefined
}
